title: W05b: bounded detail, thread and history reads
description: Implement detail, thread and history reads with the pagination and consistency rules of plan 10.3: default page size 100 and maximum 200, additionally bounded by response size; threads ordered by parsed created_at with the exact message ID as tie-breaker and reply IDs preserved without assuming the parent is on the same page; event history in canonical append order with a stable offset or identity so equal timestamps never reorder it; opaque cursors encoding version, ledger identity, collection revision, query and last key, refused when reused for another project, query or collection; a cursor_stale result when relevant content changed; a single over-limit body served through bounded detail chunks or failing clearly, with every truncated summary linking to full detail; and the response revision reported so a client can distinguish a newer view from its last board snapshot. Detect observed external edits with before and after fingerprints and refuse unstable reads. Implementation baseline: merged main 6276d5f / ledger closure e64d4bd, Waystation 0.6.0 on Bun 1.4.1; see docs/reconciliation-2026-09-27.md. Reuse the merged foundation and its tests. Reuse W05a's read snapshot/revision machinery and the W04 reconciliation/transfer event contracts. Own core cursor/detail behavior only; W06c exposes it and W08c consumes it. Preserve full source descriptions through the detail/chunk path.
acceptance: Pagination is stable across a large fixture: no record is skipped or duplicated, and a cursor from one project, query or collection is refused in another.
A relevant content change returns cursor_stale instead of silently skipping or repeating rows.
Equal-timestamp history preserves canonical append order, and a reply whose parent is off-page is still resolvable.
Large commit messages and message bodies are served in bounded chunks or fail clearly, never silently truncated.
Lifecycle inconsistencies in otherwise readable records surface as integrity diagnostics and are never presented as actionable work.
notes:
Best-effort detection of non-cooperating manual edits is the goal, not proof that every writer participated in the lock.
